baseline: Direct reading remains the baseline for short timelines. AI remains optional and unverified.

answers: Structure/ID/quote validation can prove contract/reference validity, not semantic truth. A real citation can still be false, malicious, irrelevant or insufficient to support a claim.
Embeddings are comparable only inside the same vector-space definition: model/digest, dimensions and chunk/index version. Changes to those require reindexing.

Missing semantic results should be diagnosed through scope/publication, coverage, vector-space identity and ranking. Recall@5 asks whether the relevant result was found in the top five; MRR measures how high the first relevant result ranked.
DB connections are released during inference for efficiency. Membership, revision and publication are revalidated automatically afterwards because they can change while inference runs.

Fixed-context removes retrieval from the equation and isolates generation/interpretation/validation. End-to-end covers retrieval plus generation. Abstain when evidence is missing, conflicting or insufficient.

Repeated live trials measure consistency/variability. Fresh held-out cases provide evidence of generalization; once used for tuning they are no longer fresh. Repeating known fixtures does not establish general quality.
`flag=false` means software is configured not to do something; an enforced egress boundary prevents it even if code attempts it. A process guard is not an OS/native/child-process sandbox.

Optional AI is justified only by measurable value over the deterministic/direct-reading baseline, such as time saved or better information discovery while maintaining grounding, abstention and acceptable latency. User feedback is evaluation evidence and grants no operational authority.
architectureFlows: Published runbook → chunking → pinned embeddings → indexed storage → semantic query → scoped/publication filtering → ranked results. Embeddings rank similarity; SQL/application authorization controls visibility.

Question + retrieved sources → Qwen generation → deterministic structure/ID/quote validation → current membership/revision/publication recheck → unverified display. Generated output remains untrusted.
seniorStaffScenarios: I would reject automatic incident closure based solely on convincing cited AI text. Valid citation does not equal truth; incident state/transitions remain governed by deterministic authorization and application rules. AI may propose a resolution but must not acquire operational authority.

For a new model that improves the aggregate benchmark but regresses Spanish retrieval or abstention, I would run a paired experiment on fresh held-out cases, same criteria and repeated executions, comparing language-specific retrieval, grounding, semantic failures, abstention and variability rather than relying on one aggregate score.
